school: 春秋末期思想家，道家学派创始人，周守藏室之史（周王室典籍档案管理官员）
historical_significance: 老子（约前571-约前471），姓李名耳，字聃，楚国苦县厉乡曲仁里人（一说陈国相人），春秋末期思想家、道家学派创始人。他长期担任周王室守藏室之史，掌管王室典籍与档案，遍览三代兴衰之记录，这使他成为那个时代极少见的'从最完整的失败档案中思考'的人。孔子曾适周问礼于老子，老子以'良贾深藏若虚，君子盛德容貌若愚'相告，并告诫去除骄气与多欲——这段问答见于《史记·老子韩非列传》。晚年周室衰微、王子朝之乱使典籍流散，老子遂去周西行，过函谷关时，关令尹喜请求著书，'乃著书上下篇五千余言，言道德之意'，即《道德经》（《老子》）五千言，随后出关，'莫知其所终'。《道德经》是中国哲学史上第一部系统性的形而上学著作：提出'道'为万物本原（'道生一，一生二，二生三，三生万物'），主张'道法自然''无为而治''上善若水''柔弱胜刚强''知足不辱''祸兮福之所倚'，以逆向否定的思维方式质疑儒家的仁义礼智与世俗的价值排序。其思想经庄子发扬、黄老之术入汉初治国实践（文景之治），又远播形成道教，成为唯一可与儒家在官方意识形态层面长期抗衡的中国本土思想体系。他的'守柔、处下、不争、无为'思维模式，是对强权逻辑与进取伦理的系统反命题。
historical_significance_en: Laozi (c. 571-c. 471 BCE), personal name Li Er, courtesy name Dan, born in Cu Ren Li, Lixiang, Kuxian in Chu (traditionally), was a late-Spring-and-Autumn thinker and founder of Daoism. He long served as Scribe of the Royal Archive (zhou shoucang shi zhi shi) of the Zhou royal house, custodian of the dynasty's records and documents. Having read through the complete failure archives of three dynasties, he became one of the rare thinkers of his age who reasoned from the most complete record of collapse. Confucius visited Zhou to ask him about ritual; Laozi told him 'the good merchant hides his wealth as if empty, and the gentleman of abundant virtue wears the look of a fool,' urging him to shed arrogance and desire—a dialogue preserved in the Shiji. In his later years, as the Zhou house declined and the库藏 of records scattered during the succession revolt of Prince Chao, Laozi left for the west. At the Hangu Pass the keeper Yin Xi asked him to write down his thoughts, and he 'composed a book in two parts of over five thousand characters on the meaning of Dao and De'—the Dao De Jing—then passed through the gate and 'no one knows where he ended.' The Dao De Jing is the first systematic work of metaphysics in Chinese philosophy: it posits Dao as the origin of all things ('Dao gives birth to One, One to Two, Two to Three, Three to the ten thousand things'), advocates 'Dao follows nature,' 'governing by non-action,' 'the highest good is like water,' 'the soft overcomes the hard,' 'knowing contentment averts disgrace,' and 'misfortune is what fortune leans on,' systematically inverting Confucian value hierarchies through negative, reverse-direction reasoning. Developed by Zhuangzi, practiced in the Huang-Lao statecraft of the early Han (Rule of Wen and Jing), and later institutionalized as religious Daoism, his thought is the only native Chinese system that contested Confucianism at the level of official ideology. His modes—yielding, low-positioning, non-contention, non-action—are a systematic counter-proposition to the logic of power and the ethic of striving.
description_zh: 守藏室之史的思维原型：从三代兴衰的完整档案中提炼'反者道之动'——以柔克刚、以退为进、以不争争天下之不可争，把'不做'本身锻造成最高级的'做'。
description_en: The prototype of the archivist-thinker: distilling 'reversal is the movement of Dao' from the complete failure archives of three dynasties—overcoming hardness with softness, advancing by yielding, contending for what no one contends for, and forging 'not doing' itself into the highest form of 'doing.'
roles_en: Scribe of the Zhou Royal Archive

key_concepts: 道法自然（道的运行以自身为法则）
无为而治（不妄为的治理）
上善若水（处下、利万物而不争）
反者道之动（对立面相互转化）
祸福相倚（事物的辩证转化）
知足知止（知足不辱，知止不殆）
大巧若拙（大直若屈，大辩若讷）
小国寡民（低复杂度社会理想）
有无相生（'有'之利在'无'处生成）
quote: 上善若水。水善利万物而不争，处众人之所恶，故几于道。——《道德经》第八章
quote_en: The highest good is like water. Water benefits the ten thousand things and does not contend; it dwells in the places people disdain—thereby it comes near to Dao. (Dao De Jing, ch. 8)
